units.translation: 1-5a. Now, goddess, the toil: the particle “O” is omitted, so that it would be “O goddess.” The sense: now tell me yourself, O Muse, both the toil and the counsels of Medea, since I am at a loss, so as not to be able to say whether it was through erotic passion or by making an escape from ill-treatment that she left her fatherland.
3 the words which follow ἀποροῦντός μου L presents both in this place and attached to scholion b, where W deleted them (Phil. 81, 1926, 21) ὥστε — εἰπεῖν in L² : omitted in L¹ : differently in P

b. Or for me at least with speechlessness: instead of “with perplexity,” “with speechlessness.”
7. Upon them: dative instead of accusative; for it is not “among them.” Lg

8. Upon his spirit with a hateful contest: he called the contest hateful, at which he himself was gloomy and distressed.
οὐ in K : οὕτως
11. Most painful: either by addition of the ε; for it is “most painful,” derived from “to suffer pain.” Or it is said to mean “having cares,” so that the word is from “to care for.”

12. And she trembled like some: a κεμάς is a young deer. They say there is a difference between a κεμάς and a fawn: for a κεμάς is one still sleeping in the cave, being as it were a “sleeper” (κοιμάς), while a fawn is one already larger and going out to pasture and feeding.

13 Et. Gen. (AB) κεμάς: . . . IV 12—13. κεμάς (δὲ add. B) is the newborn deer. They say there is a difference between a κεμάς and a fawn: for a κεμάς is one still (sch., ἐπὶ AB) sleeping in the cave, while a fawn is one larger and feeding on pasture. . . . sch. II 696 sch. B K 361 Apoll. Lex. Hom. 97, 33 B. Hesych. κεμάς Συν. κ. (273, 11 Ba. Phot. Suid.) Eust. 811, 37

13. In thickets: in dense places. Lg (P)

14. He thought: from the verb “οἴω” comes “ὀίω” by diaeresis 〈...〉. Perhaps also “δοάσσατο” (Homer) uses the δ redundantly, as also “δνοφερὸν ὕδωρ” (Homer); for it is formed from “νέφος.” And from “ἷψαι” Sophocles in Ixion (fr. 296 Pearson) says “δίψιον”
